questions.prompt: What must the root layout (app/layout.tsx) render that nested layouts do not?
questions.explanation: The root layout is the document shell, so it must render <html> and <body>. Nested layouts may omit them.

questions.prompt: Which prop does a layout render to show the nested page or layout inside it?
questions.explanation: Layouts receive a children prop and must render it; that is where the nested content appears.

questions.prompt: You navigate between /dashboard and /dashboard/settings, which share a dashboard layout. What happens to that layout?

options.text: It stays mounted and does not re-render, preserving its state
It fully re-mounts on each navigation
It is removed and the page renders alone
It reloads the whole browser page

questions.explanation: Shared layouts persist across navigation between their child routes — only the changed segment re-renders, so layout state is preserved.

questions.prompt: Which statements about layouts are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: A layout.tsx wraps its segment and everything nested under it
Layouts are Server Components by default
You can freely use useState in a layout without any directive

questions.explanation: Layouts wrap nested segments, are Server Components by default, and templates re-mount per navigation. useState requires a Client Component ("use client").

questions.prompt: Match each file to its role.

pairs.right: Root layout: renders <html>/<body>, wraps every page
Section layout: wraps only /dashboard and its children
Like a layout but re-mounts on each navigation
The UI for a single route

questions.explanation: The root layout is the document shell; a nested layout scopes shared UI to a section; a template re-mounts per navigation; a page renders one route.

questions.prompt: Order these layers from outermost to innermost when rendering /dashboard/settings.
questions.explanation: Layouts nest from the root down: the root layout wraps the dashboard layout, which wraps the settings page via its children.
